The story describes The bourbon bottle like this: From the file cabinet bottom drawer. Half-empty in the way a half-empty bottle is half-empty when nobody else has been pouring. The bottle of bourbon at his elbow looked, suddenly, less like a bad decision and more like a tool whose specific function he was about to need. He uncapped it. Poured one finger into the chipped glass on the desk. Drank it. Half-empty in the way half-empty bottles are half-empty when only one man has been pouring from them. He poured himself a bourbon. Neat. No ice. Ice was for the weak. Ice diluted the truth of the thing. He left the bottle uncapped, because uncapping it had always felt like a commitment and recapping it had always felt like a lie, and he had stopped lying to bottles in 2017.
